input.brief: Vettri HRMS: HR, payroll and company-laptop management in one app for Indian companies of 20 to 500 people

direction.name: The printed annual
direction.idea: Lay the page out like a well-designed printed report or magazine feature: a masthead image, a tight oversized title, text held to a strict column line, and colour used in solid blocks the way a two-colour print job would. It gives weight and authority to subjects that are really about content: findings, a manifesto, a programme, a serious product. The reader should feel that someone edited this.
direction.composition: A fixed vertical axis at about 42% of the viewport width organises everything: headings begin on it, body columns hang from it, and the 0–42% zone holds small side notes, figures or stays empty. Masthead: a wide image band (photographic mosaic or a single crop) across the top 45% of the first screen; below it the title at 7–9vw starting on the axis, with a two-sentence standfirst at 20–24px. Sections alternate between text pages (title on the axis, body in one or two columns of 34–40ch to its right) and full-bleed colour pages carrying one large figure, quotation or image mosaic. Mosaics are gutterless: photographs and flat colour tiles butted together in a 4- or 6-cell grid. Page numbers, running heads and other print furniture are left out.
direction.typography: A tight heavy grotesk or a sharp serif for titles; an excellent text face for reading at 18–20px with leading near 1.5. Headings in sentence case, tracked tight.
direction.colour: Paper, ink and two or three solid block colours. A colour page is a whole section in one flat colour.
direction.imagery: Photographs used as blocks in mosaics alongside flat colour tiles; mixed subjects are fine if cropped tight and converted to one treatment.
direction.photoTreatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.
direction.richness: The column line, the mosaics and whole pages of colour give structure and variety without ornaments.
direction.pitfalls: The axis must be exact and reused everywhere or it reads as random indentation. Keep paragraphs to a real reading measure. On a phone the axis collapses to the left margin and side notes move inline above their paragraph.

hero.name: Void, then statement on axis
hero.blueprint: A deliberate void: the upper 60% of the viewport holds nothing but the top row. That row, 44px from the top on 48px margins, has the wordmark at the left margin, two text links starting exactly on a vertical axis at 42% of the width, and the single action at the right margin as a text link. Everything else hangs from the same axis in the bottom third. The statement starts on the 42% line: two lines at clamp(56px, 6.6vw, 104px), regular or medium weight, tracking -0.04em, leading 0.95, running towards the right margin, with its last baseline 72px above the bottom edge. Left of the axis, in columns 1-4, one supporting sentence at 18px in the soft ink, max 32ch, is bottom-aligned to the statement's last baseline. Nothing sits in the left zone above it. No image and no shape; the ground is one flat tone and the ink one colour. The emptiness is composed: three elements share the axis, so the blank area reads as intended and not as a page that failed to load.
hero.mobile: The axis collapses to the 20px left margin. The top 48% of the screen stays empty under the wordmark row. The statement sets at 12.5vw on two lines, flush left, followed by the sentence at 17px and the action as a text link, the whole block ending 28px above the bottom edge. The two links fold behind a menu word.
hero.headline: A 3-6 word statement, at most 30 characters over two lines, about 15 per line at 6.6vw from the axis.

type.note: A grotesk with slightly geometric bowls, set bold and very large against plain 16px text with nothing in between. Suits studios, type and product launches, and finance or tech brands that lead with the name.

palette.name: Blush and aubergine
palette.note: Blush pink and dark aubergine alternate as full fields and serve as each other's text colour, in roughly equal shares. There is no third colour: the button is a solid block of whichever of the two is not the ground.

photos.title: Architecture
photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors
photos.treatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.

photos.alt: Silhouetted people at tall windows overlooking a city, black and white
Curving glass and steel lattice roof in black and white
White apartment block facade with repeating balconies and windows
Tall pointed vaults and pale columns of a church interior

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Input half, output half
sections.blueprint: Two flat fields meet on a vertical edge at 50vw, each 90svh tall, no gap. The left field is the darkest palette tone and holds what the user hands the product, raw: a pasted note, a messy row of figures, a prompt, or literal code inside `<code>`. It is an editable region at 20–24px, 34ch wide, starting at column 2, 30% down the field. The right field is the lightest tone and holds what the product makes of it as a true-size fragment marked data-ui: the tidy record, the chart, the formatted reply, 440–520px wide, on the same top line. Editing the left changes the right. The heading is split across the edge: its first one or two words bottom-left on the dark field, its last one or two bottom-right on the light field, both at clamp(40px, 5vw, 80px) on one baseline 32px from the bottom.
sections.mobile: The fields stack, dark above light, each 62svh, meeting on a horizontal edge. Input text at 18px with 20px margins; the output fragment at true size on the light field. The heading's two parts sit either side of that edge at 11vw: one at the foot of the dark field, one at the top of the light.

sections.name: Rows with margin photographs
sections.blueprint: Everything hangs from one vertical axis at column 5, about 35% of the width. First the heading: a statement of up to five words at clamp(40px, 5vw, 80px) starting on the axis, vertically centred in an otherwise empty 70svh of ground. Then four or five benefit rows, each starting on the same axis: a title at clamp(28px, 3vw, 48px) and under it a paragraph of 34ch at 17px. Columns 1–4 stay empty. At the right margin each row carries one photograph, top-aligned with its title and deliberately unequal: 240px wide at 4:5 in one row, 320px at 3:2 in the next, 180px square after that. Rows are separated by 96–120px of space, not lines. On a saturated field, set all type in one pale ink and leave the photographs ungraded.
sections.mobile: The axis collapses to the left margin. The statement sits at 9vw in 50svh of empty ground. Each row stacks its title at 26px, the paragraph, then its photograph at alternating widths: 100%, 70% flush right, 55% flush left. 64px between rows.

sections.name: Stages as one bar
sections.blueprint: The product's progress bar, enlarged until it spans the page, is the diagram. One bar runs across columns 1–12, 22vh tall, built as a flex row of three or four solid segments with 6px gaps, root marked data-ui. Each segment's width follows how long that stage really takes (flex-grow from the true durations, 12% minimum), and each is a different flat palette colour, so the reader sees at once that signing up is a sliver and the rest is the product working. Inside every segment, top-left with 20px padding, its duration in words at clamp(20px, 2vw, 30px): 'Two minutes', 'About a day'. Under each segment, on its left edge, one clause at 17px, 22ch wide, beginning with its order word. Above the bar, 64px clear of it, the heading: two to five words at clamp(48px, 6.4vw, 104px), flush left. Nothing else.
sections.mobile: The bar turns vertical: segments stack as full-width blocks whose heights keep the proportions, 72px minimum, 6px gaps, about 70svh in total. Each holds its duration at 22px top-left and its clause at 16px beneath. The heading sits above at 11vw on two lines.

sections.name: Recognition as a table
sections.blueprint: Awards, press mentions or credits set as a four-column table with no lines. The heading is two or three words at about 5vw, stepped over two lines with the second line indented by two columns, and occupies columns 1–7. The table begins 72px below and spans columns 1–12 on a fixed grid: year in columns 1–2, project or title in 3–6, awarding body or publication in 7–10, the award itself in 11–12, right-aligned. Rows are set at 16–17px with 14px of padding above and below; every second row carries a background tone one step from the ground, running the full table width, which replaces rules. Year groups are separated by one blank row, and the year is printed only on the first row of its group. Use a real `<table>` with `border-collapse: collapse` and no borders.
sections.mobile: The heading drops to 11vw. Each table row becomes a two-line block: title on the first line in the full ink, then body and award on the second in the softer ink. The year stands once as a 22px figure above its group. Alternate blocks keep the background tone.

sections.name: Two plans, two fields
sections.blueprint: Two plans stand side by side as two full-height colour fields that meet at a hard vertical edge with no gap: the left field spans columns 1–5, the right 6–12, both 90svh tall and bleeding to the viewport edges. Each field has its own flat colour and its assigned text colour. Inside each, on a shared grid: the plan name at about 5vw top-left with 40px padding; one sentence at 20px beneath it, no wider than 26ch, saying who the plan is for; then, anchored to the bottom-left, the price at about 10vw with the period at 18px beside it; and a rectangular button anchored bottom-right on the price's baseline. What is included is written as a short paragraph, not a tick list. The unequal widths say which plan matters more without any badge. No heading spans the two fields.
sections.mobile: The fields stack, each 70svh tall, the more important plan first. Name at 12vw top-left, sentence beneath, price at 24vw at the bottom-left, and the button full width along the bottom edge inside 20px padding. The hard colour edge between the two is kept.

sections.name: Answers as reading text
sections.blueprint: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
sections.mobile: One column at 16px with 20px margins. The heading leads at 24px. Each paragraph keeps its run-in question in the medium weight, with 18px between paragraphs. The section may run to two screens; do not collapse it into an accordion.

sections.name: Three photographs, then a field
sections.blueprint: Two parts with no gap between them. First, a strip of three photographs butted edge to edge across the full viewport, each one third wide and 40svh tall, `object-fit: cover`, no gutters and no captions; give all three the same treatment. Directly beneath, a band in one flat palette colour, about 44svh tall. In the band, columns 1–7: the closing statement at 26–30px over three lines in the band's assigned ink, with exactly one phrase underlined by a 4px bar (`text-decoration-thickness: 4px; text-underline-offset: 6px`), and that phrase is the link; two lines at 16px follow 32px lower. In the lower-right corner, columns 11–12, a small portrait photograph (4:5, about 150px wide) sits 40px from the band's edges: the person who will answer. There is no button; the underlined phrase is the action.
sections.mobile: The strip becomes one full-width photograph at 4:3 with the other two side by side beneath it at half width each, still gutterless. The band follows: statement at 22px, the two small lines, and the portrait at 96px wide in the bottom-right corner.

sections.name: Contact as the headline
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed field in one saturated palette colour, at least 90svh tall. Top row, 40px from the edge: two or three short notes at 15px in columns 1–7 (address, hours, a one-line description) and a back-to-top text link at the right margin. Then a tall empty gap. In the lower half, the way to get in touch is the display line: the telephone number or the email address itself, set at 8–9vw, flush left, hard against the margin, as one link. An email address may break once, before the @, giving two lines. Size it with `clamp()` so the longest line fills at least 80% of the width. Under it, one row of small text at 14px spread across three positions: links at the left, credits in the centre, city and year at the right. The wordmark appears only small, in the top row.
sections.mobile: Notes stack at the top at 15px. The contact line sits in the lower half at 12vw; a telephone number stays on one line, an email breaks before the @ and is sized so each half fits the width. The meta row becomes three stacked lines at 13px.

references.name: Artem Taradash
references.idea: A designer's CV compressed into one newspaper-like band at the top, after which oversized product renders and project artefacts speak at full scale.
references.hero: White page with 20px margins. Top-left are three small black rectangular tags with white text (name and two links). Below them a three-line statement at about 3vw in regular-weight grotesk fills the first third, left-aligned. To its right, starting at the very top edge, run two narrow columns of 12px text, then a third column listing clients one per line, and in the far top-right a circular portrait about 200px wide with a white hand-lettered word across the face. This text band ends by a quarter of the height. Below it a huge cut-out vehicle render bleeds off the bottom, with a project card at right.
references.type: One family, Diatype, in regular weight throughout. Three sizes: about 43px for statements and project titles, 12.4px for all running text, about 11px for tags. Tight leading, sentence case, no bold and no capitals; hierarchy comes from size alone.
references.colour: #ffffff #111111 #f7f9fb #1c4fd8 #f0a23a — Strictly black on white for the frame. All colour arrives with project material: an orange-to-blue gradient, a cobalt zigzag pattern, warm photography.
references.imagery: Product renders cut out on white and shown very large, interface screenshots with a small corner radius, a full-width studio photo with a circular logo overlaid, and textile-pattern fields running margin to margin. Scale varies sharply between projects.
references.layout: A loose six-column grid with 20px margins; small text blocks hang from column lines beside very large images. Each project is arranged differently, and there are no dividers or section backgrounds, only white space and jumps in scale. The tag nav stays fixed top-left.

sections.description: Each project pairs one oversized visual with a small caption cluster. In the first, a cut-out product render fills the left 60% and bleeds off the edge. The right third stacks a landscape screenshot with slightly rounded corners, then a row holding a tiny label and two-line title at about 3vw on the left and a five-line 12px description on the right.

A row of three: a round black watch-face mock-up about a quarter of the width, a wide rectangle filled with a horizontal blue, violet, orange, blue gradient with a tiny tick scale beneath it, and a narrow text column at far right with label, three-line title and two short paragraphs. Circle, rectangle and text share a top line.

A cobalt-and-white zigzag textile pattern runs margin to margin for more than a full viewport height with only a two-line caption beneath it at left. Before it, a black-backed mosaic of pattern samples and report-cover mock-ups sits beside two narrow text columns. The pattern is given a section to itself with no mock-up frame.

Closing row on white: a tiny label, then a four-line sentence at about 3vw in the left third; a small square portrait at the two-thirds mark; to its right a short question with two underlined links below. All three hang from the same top line with empty space between them.

steal: Put bio, client list and portrait in one compact multi-column band at the top so the first scroll is already work.
Use solid black rectangular tags with white text as the only navigation chrome.
Let one project artefact (a pattern, a gradient) run full width for a whole screen with a two-line caption instead of framing it in a mock-up.

references.name: Applied Imagination
references.idea: An essay conceived on a flight is read as a descent: an altimeter ticks from 30,000 ft to zero while you scroll down through halftone clouds to mountains at ground level.
references.hero: A pale blue sky fading to warm cream fills the viewport, with white clouds shaded in halftone dots. A tiny serif logotype sits top-centre; no nav. The title, two centred lines of black wedge-serif at 8.9vw, occupies the middle half of the screen and about 73% of its width; a cloud layer passes in front of the second line's baseline so the feet of the letters dissolve into dots. A two-line centred deck at 24px sits beneath. A mono byline strip is centred on the bottom edge with a scroll cue bottom-right. On the left edge at mid-height, a short vertical rule carries a two-line mono altitude readout.
references.type: fsKim, a sturdy wedge-serif display face, regular weight at 128px with -0.01em tracking for the title and pull quotes; gtAmerica at 24px for the deck and about 16px for essay body; gtAmericaMono uppercase around 11px with wide tracking for byline, altitude and tape labels.
references.colour: #cbe4f2 #f1e3b5 #0a0a0a #ffc013 #8e2f8f #f04e23 — Sky blue melting into sand yellow is the constant ground and text is black. Saturated magenta, orange and yellow arrive only in collage objects, tape labels and the footer contact card.
references.imagery: Photo-collage cut-outs (parachutes carrying a treasure chest and a burning dumpster, a pair of legs, mountains) given a coarse halftone dot screen, layered in front of and behind the type against painted clouds.
references.layout: A narrow text column about 38% wide for essay passages, interrupted by full-width display pull quotes and collage objects floating at the edges. One continuous sky instead of sections, with a fixed left-edge altimeter. Nearly 23 screens, ending on a ground-level landscape.

sections.description: Sky background, no container. A three-line pull quote in black wedge-serif at about 7vw is centred and tightly leaded. Two cut-out parachutes hang over it: a magenta one from the top-left carrying a chest spilling coins, an orange one at lower right carrying a burning dumpster, each overlapping letterforms. Small mono labels on tilted strips of coloured tape are stuck to the objects. Words in the quote turn from grey to black as they are reached.

Running essay text in about 16px grotesk, black, in a single column roughly 38% of the viewport wide, positioned left of centre with large sky margins on both sides. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line; serif sub-statements at about 28px introduce passages. The next display quote is seen rising from below, its letters partly hidden behind cloud and blurred.

Ground level: halftone-screened mountains in green and brown rise from both sides, and the title returns at huge scale, cropped by the top edge and tucked behind the peaks. Centred below is a square-cornered two-panel card: a cream left panel with a short form of two fields and a small orange button, and a magenta right panel with a round portrait, name and a yellow subscribe button. Yellow tape-strip credits sit on the bottom edge.

steal: Tie a persistent numeric readout to scroll position (altitude falling to zero) so the reader's progress becomes part of the story.
Layer an illustration element in front of the bottom of a giant title so the letters sink into the scene instead of sitting on top.
Apply one coarse halftone dot screen to every photo cut-out so collage pieces from different sources read as one illustration set.

references.name: Vessa
references.idea: A brand-guidelines tool that frames its live demo inside an electric-blue dithered pixel field and marks the whole page with dashed artboard guides and corner handles.
references.hero: Pale cool-grey page with dashed vertical guides about 2% in from each edge. A soft blue halftone arc of pixels glows behind the top nav: logo left, four links centre, sign-in and a blue button right. Centred below: a two-line medium-weight headline at 3.9vw with very tight tracking, about 43% of viewport width; three lines of 18px grey text with one bold phrase; a small blue button with 6px corners; a pill counter. At 58% down a full-width electric-blue block begins, its fill breaking into checker dither at the top, with small square handles at its corners; inside, a pill tab bar and the top of a black demo page.
references.type: Switzer only: weight 500 at 56px with -0.045em tracking for the headline, about 18px regular for lead text, 15px body, 13px nav. Section headings drop to roughly 28px, so the hero is the single large moment. Emphasis by bold or blue text, never capitals.
references.colour: #eef0f3 #1f2de6 #010101 #f5f6f8 #ffffff — Cool pale grey with one electric blue used for buttons, one highlighted sentence and large dithered frames; the embedded demo brings black and warm photographic tones.
references.imagery: Live product demo pages (a fictional sports brand with a dramatic runner photo, logo lockups on white and black) sit as rounded panels inside blue ordered-dither pixel frames; small grey-and-blue schematic diagrams elsewhere.
references.layout: A container of about 1300px bounded by dashed guide lines that continue down the page and split into dashed grid cells for features. Centred text sections alternate with left-aligned split rows and full-width blue dithered blocks, separated by generous vertical gaps.

sections.description: Centred column about 55% of viewport width set in roughly 22px regular text as three or four short paragraphs with wide gaps and no heading. The final one-line paragraph switches to the accent blue as the turn of the argument. No images, cards or rules; only the dashed side guides frame it.

Two-column row. Left: a blue dithered rectangle about 45% of the width whose solid centre dissolves to pixels at the edges, containing a small white rounded card with a schematic of a URL turning into colour swatches and a font tag. Right: a pill stepper of three tabs with an arrow button, then a small bold title and four lines of 14px text placed mid-height. The section title sits far below at left in 28px.

A grid drawn only with dashed lines. First a full-width cell with a centred diagram of five small bordered chips hanging from a blue tag by dashed connectors, title and text at bottom left. Below it two cells side by side, each with a grey-and-blue schematic (scattered rounded squares; an input wired to a browser strip) in the upper two thirds and a bold one-line title plus three lines of small text at the bottom left.

Full-width blue dithered block with corner handles; in its middle a solid blue rectangle about half the width holds a centred two-line white heading at 28px and a small white button. Directly below sits the footer: brand blurb and a directory badge at left, five link columns separated by dashed vertical rules, and a one-line legal strip under a dashed horizontal rule.

steal: Replace gradient backgrounds with an ordered-dither pixel pattern in the accent colour that dissolves from solid to checkerboard at the edges.
Use dashed guide lines and small square corner handles as the page's structural ornament, including as dividers between feature cells and footer columns.
Embed the real product with its own tab bar directly under the hero copy instead of a static screenshot.
